correctness.rationale: The proof reduces circular universality on a 2k+1 cycle exactly to a matching of size k in the unequal-edge graph, then to a unique even-length path after equal-edge deletion. The multinomial/stars-and-bars count preserves marked-edge multiplicities, all colorings satisfy cyclic parity, coprime symbol contents prove primitive rotations, and fixed-reflection edge choices give the bracelet count. Boundary k=1 is explicit. Independently written exhaustive tests compare 174760 binary words with greedy arch recognition, 680 with direct subsequence enumeration, and verify orbit counts for k=1..8; experiments support but do not prove the infinite result.

value.rationale: At the first nonminimal length of binary circular subsequence universality, the theorem identifies every feasible cyclic word via a locally checkable parity criterion and gives exact design-space counts under labeled, rotational and dihedral equivalence for all k. The structural cycle-matching reduction and explicit reflection count address natural information-compression symmetries, not a chosen arbitrary finite slice. Existing tools for deciding universality do not automatically supply these enumeration and rigidity statements.
